form_fields.incident_location_description: I want to be clear about why I'm leaving this blank instead of guessing. The thing that hurt me is a pressure cooker, and the actual incident — the lid blowing off and the contents going across the kitchen and the burn happening — happened in a kitchen. But I'm in the middle of a separation from my husband Brennan and during the period when this happened I was staying at three different places depending on the week. Two nights at my mother's house in Mesa, three or four nights at my friend Tomasina's casita in Gilbert, and the rest at the apartment Brennan and I were still technically sharing in Chandler. The pressure cooker incident happened on a Thursday evening and I genuinely cannot remember which house I was at that night. I think it was my mother's because I remember her dog being upset by the noise but I am not 100 percent certain and I don't want to put down an address that turns out to be wrong. I will figure this out — I can probably reconstruct it from texts or from when I posted in my recipe group — but I didn't want to put a wrong address on a legal form.

content.narrative_block:
I was making a beef stew on April 2nd, a Thursday evening, around 7:15pm. The cooker is a Hearthwell ProSeal 6-Quart Multi-Cooker, model HW-PS6, which I bought new from a Costco in Tempe in November 2024 — I have the receipt because I save everything in a shoebox in the closet. I had used it maybe 30 or 35 times before that night. I followed the recipe in the included cookbook for beef stew on the 'High Pressure' setting, 35 minutes. I locked the lid the way I always do — there's a hard click and a little arrow that lines up with a triangle on the body. The pressure indicator was up. The cooker was beeping along normally. About 22 minutes into the cook I was reading at the kitchen counter maybe four feet away when there was a loud bang and the lid came off straight up — it dented the underside of the upper cabinet — and the contents sprayed in basically a fountain. Most of the broth and beef and onions hit me on the right arm, the right side of my chest, and the right side of my neck and jaw. I was wearing a thin cotton shirt and the broth went through it instantly.

I screamed and ran to the sink and started running cool water over my arm. I was alone. I called 911 from my phone, which I had to wipe off because it was covered in stew. EMS came within probably eight minutes. They were Mesa Fire and Medical (I remember the patch said Mesa) and the paramedic in charge was a woman named Helena something — I want to say Helena Vasquez but I'm not sure. They cut my shirt off, irrigated the burns, wrapped me, and took me to Banner Desert Medical Center because the burn unit there is the closest. (This is part of why I think it was my mother's house — Banner Desert is the natural hospital from Mesa, not from Chandler or Gilbert.) I was admitted overnight. The burn team assessed me as second-degree partial thickness over approximately 9% of my body, mostly the right arm and the right side of the torso and neck, with a small area of third-degree on the inner right forearm where the skin actually came off. The third-degree spot is about the size of a credit card.

I was in the hospital for two nights. Since then I've had follow-ups every week at the Banner Desert burn clinic with Dr. Eustace Pickering. I'm on hydrocodone for breakthrough pain and gabapentin because the nerve pain is what's actually the worst part — it's a constant low-grade screaming that gets worse at night. They've talked about a skin graft for the third-degree area but want to give it another four to six weeks to see if it heals on its own. The scarring on the rest of my arm and neck is going to be permanent according to Dr. Pickering. I'm 37 years old (well, I'd rather give my exact birthday to a real person on the phone, I'm a little paranoid about putting it in a web form — I'll give it to whoever calls me back, sorry) and the cosmetic side of this is hitting me hard. I work as a high school theater teacher and I'm supposed to be visible and confident in front of teenagers all day.

I still have the cooker. It's in a plastic bin in my mother's garage. I didn't wash it. The lid is in there too — the gasket was found across the room, partly melted. The Hearthwell company has a customer service line and I called them once, in tears, on April 4th from the hospital. The woman I spoke to (her name was Marigold — I remember thinking that was a beautiful name even through everything) was nice but immediately offered me a replacement cooker and a $100 gift card. I told her I'd been hospitalized and she said someone from their 'safety review' department would call me back. Nobody has. That was six weeks ago. That's the moment my sister-in-law Coraline told me I needed to call a lawyer.

What I have: the original Costco receipt, the cookbook and manual that came with the cooker, the cooker itself with the lid and gasket, photos I took of the kitchen ceiling and cabinet damage (my friend Tomasina took these the next morning, I was not in shape to do it that night), the EMS report I requested last week, the Banner Desert admission paperwork and all the discharge summaries, all the burn clinic visit notes, my pharmacy records, and the call log on my phone showing the calls to 911 and to Hearthwell on April 4th. I have not posted anything about this on social media because Coraline told me not to.

I think this thing is dangerous. I went online after I got home and there's a Reddit thread with eight or nine people describing almost the exact same thing happening with the same cooker model. I didn't reply or comment but I screenshotted the thread. I want to know what my options are.

The only things I haven't been able to give you in this form are which house this happened at — I will get you the actual address as soon as I confirm it from my texts, probably tomorrow morning — and my date of birth, which I'd rather give the attorney directly on the phone. I'll have both for you when you call.
